rationale.product_understanding: analysis.md lines 9-21 separate supplied limits from illustrative prices, dates, tax and cancellation policy, and the role model is explicit. The interface labels simulated payments and estimated tax instead of claiming a real charge. Only confirmation of the refund and over-limit policies would sharpen it.
rationale.ux_reasoning: The summary answers plan, price, renewal, next payment and 12/20 members, then billing, member limits, invoices and an isolated cancellation zone (evidence/subscription-settings-r3/a/summary.png). Blocked downgrades, period changes and the next-invoice breakdown all expose consequences before confirmation. The owner journey is coherent from summary to destructive action.
rationale.design_judgment: Changes are scheduled at renewal, downgrades over the limit are hard-blocked, cancellation is separated and the safe action is primary. The optional cancellation reason and labelled 9% tax estimate are transparent rather than deceptive. The decision to give each billing concern its own card adds length, but the trade-off is defensible.
rationale.visual_hierarchy: Desktop summary and billing cards are well composed, but the floating prototype pill covers the 'Update payment method' button (evidence/subscription-settings-r3/a/payment-button-overlap.png). More seriously, the mobile cancellation action sits roughly 290px below its explanatory copy (evidence/subscription-settings-r3/a/mobile-cancel-gap.png) because .cancel-copy flex-basis becomes a height in the column layout (styles.css lines 697 and 1240). Fixing both would raise this to 3 or 4.
rationale.interaction_completeness: The build implements loading, load error, empty invoices, payment-failed banner (app.js line 123), near/at-limit, blocked downgrade, scheduled change, cancellation and success states, plus validation and busy handling. The 10-state table in analysis.md lines 125-138 matches the code. A member-removal hand-off after a blocked downgrade is the remaining gap.
rationale.accessibility_responsiveness: checks.json reports two axe aria-progressbar-name violations and one definition-list violation on both viewports; the meters at app.js line 258 have aria-valuetext but no accessible name. Responsive widths are otherwise clean at 320-1280. Naming the meters and fixing the dl structure would raise this to 3.
rationale.implementation_quality: The render-function architecture and state model are consistent and the reported interaction checks pass. The mobile flex-basis bug and invalid definition list are avoidable CSS/markup defects, and the single 1548-line app.js is still a monolith. Adding layout tests for the cancellation zone and fixing semantics would raise this.

The floating prototype controls cover the Update payment method button in the desktop capture.

strengths: Most complete state coverage in the pair, including a payment-failed banner and recovery path.
Clear summary with renewal, next payment and member count in one card.
Blocked downgrade, separated cancellation and labelled simulated tax.
Explicit role banner and named owner for member view.

rationale.product_understanding: analysis.md lines 9-20 label every price, date and policy as an assumption and correctly describe the owner/member boundary, including the deliberately conservative invoice restriction. The interface never claims a real charge and explains missing downloads. The main gap is that failed-payment recovery is explicitly out of scope.
rationale.ux_reasoning: The page opens with an at-a-glance card answering plan, price, renewal and 12/20 seats (evidence/subscription-settings-r3/b/summary.png), then plans, payment, invoices and a separated cancellation section, with a persistent on-page navigator. The price-display toggle is clearly separated from a real cadence change. The 'Move to Free' action correctly routes to the cancellation review (app.js line 353 and line 1056), so there is one path to Free.
rationale.design_judgment: The analysis states explicit trade-offs (immediate versus scheduled changes, acknowledgement versus typed phrase, hiding versus locking owner controls), and the build matches them. Free is routed through cancellation with a consequence list, avoiding the competing-path problem seen elsewhere. The decision to omit failed-payment recovery is defensible only because it is declared, not hidden.
rationale.visual_hierarchy: This is the most coherent composition of the pair: a dominant price, clean section navigator, restrained colour and generous spacing; the plan cards compare cleanly (evidence/subscription-settings-r3/b/plans.png). The only visible overlap is the small demo pill over the Members row on mobile (evidence/subscription-settings-r3/b/mobile-controls-row.png), which is prototype chrome rather than product content.
rationale.interaction_completeness: Loading, load error, empty payment and invoices, success, disabled, scheduled plan/cadence states, undo, validation, busy and cancellation gating are implemented and covered by 38 assertions (analysis.md lines 120-125). There is no failed-payment or dunning state at all (analysis.md line 142), unlike Candidate A. Adding that recovery path would raise this to 4.
rationale.accessibility_responsiveness: checks.json reports one color-contrast failure on desktop and one prohibited ARIA attribute plus a contrast failure on mobile. Controls are all named and the layout stacks without overflow. Correcting the contrast pair and the prohibited attribute would raise this to 4.
rationale.implementation_quality: The 1232-line app.js and 2335-line styles.css are organised into render helpers with a clean state model and no reported console errors. The missing failed-payment state and the ARIA misuse are the main quality gaps. Adding the state and tightening semantics would raise this.

comparison: Candidate B is more visually coherent and more accessible, and routes Free through the cancellation flow, while Candidate A covers payment failure and a broader state set. Candidate A's mobile cancellation spacing bug, unnamed progressbars and control overlap outweigh its extra states, so Candidate B wins the pair.
limitations: Only default-state screenshots were supplied, so dialogs and alternate states were assessed from code and checks.json. The axe results were available as counts without node details, and no screen-reader, cross-browser, zoom or real-provider behaviour could be tested. The demo control panels are chrome, but their overlap is visible in the captures.
